prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1345; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle stopped abruptly and was struck from behind. Claimant's vehicle was stationary at the time of impact. Police report requested. Claimant advised that she is not represented by counsel at this time.

Entry 2: Contacted claimant by phone to introduce myself and confirm her contact details. Claimant reports neck and lower back pain beginning the morning after the collision. She has not yet seen a physician. Advised her of the medical payments coverage available under her policy and the process for submitting bills. Claimant stated she intends to handle the claim herself.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received from the insured. Rear bumper and trunk damage visible on the claimant's vehicle. Minor scuffing on the front of the insured vehicle. Damage appears consistent with the reported impact. Sent repair estimate request to the body shop on file. Claimant's vehicle to be inspected at the shop this week.

Entry 4: Claimant visited urgent care and was diagnosed with cervical and lumbar strain. Claimant provided the discharge summary by email and asked how long the claim review would take. Explained the typical timeline for bodily injury evaluation and that additional medical records may be needed. Requested a signed medical authorization form to obtain treatment records directly.

Entry 5: Received the signed medical authorization and the police report. Repair estimate received and reviewed. Claimant's rental vehicle coverage confirmed. Sent a follow-up letter to claimant summarizing open items: physical therapy records, wage documentation if applicable, and the final repair invoice. File remains open pending medical review.
